PatternTimeProfile.description:
How long a change of this kind takes to show up (SPEC section 7.5).

`routine_watch.patterns_library.TimeProfile` as `GET /patterns` serves it: a step
change over days and a drift over weeks are different patterns, so the window a
change has been building for is part of what the library says to look for.

onset_days.description: The onset window in days, earliest first: how long a change of this kind is expected to have been building.
onset_days.title: Onset Days

tolerance_days.description: How far outside the onset window still counts for anything.
tolerance_days.title: Tolerance Days

note.description: The phrase a nurse reads, kept next to the numbers it describes, e.g. 'a step change within 1-3 days'.
note.title: Note

PatternTimeProfile.title: PatternTimeProfile

PatternUrgency.description: How soon a pattern wants a human to look (SPEC section 7.5).
PatternUrgency.title: PatternUrgency

SuggestedCheck.description: Checks an alert may suggest to the care team (SPEC section 6.4).
SuggestedCheck.title: SuggestedCheck

description:
One entry of the pattern library (`GET /patterns`, SPEC section 7.5).

The library held as data (`routine_watch.patterns_library.LIBRARY`) as the route
reads it out: what the rule looks for and how much each signal counts, the time
profile it follows, what to rule out, how soon somebody should look, and where
the pattern comes from. A cited rules library anybody can audit, and nothing
about a resident - the scored answer for one change is `PatternMatch`.

The scoring machinery stays behind the route: which signals a pattern is defined
by, the care-record context that raises or lowers it, its confidence ceiling.
`routine_watch.patterns` owns all of that, so a reader gets the rule rather than
the arithmetic.

pattern_id.description: The pattern in the library, e.g. 'sudden_change'.
pattern_id.title: Pattern Id

name.description: How the pattern is shown to a nurse.
name.title: Name

signals.description: Signal name -> weight: what the rule looks for and how much each signal counts. The names are `routine_watch.patterns.SIGNALS`.
signals.title: Signals

checks.description: What to rule out: a shared SuggestedCheck where one fits, otherwise the pattern's own wording, exactly as `PatternMatch.checks` carries it.
checks.title: Checks

source.description: Where the pattern comes from: a SPEC section, a clinical screen, a citation. Never empty - an uncited rule is not a pattern (SPEC section 7.5).
source.title: Source

title: PatternLibraryEntry
